# A practical guide to llms.txt and AI search
URL: https://6t9xstar.github.io/velocita/blog/llms-txt-guide/

## What llms.txt is

`llms.txt` is a proposed Markdown file at the root of a site that lists its most useful pages with short descriptions, so language models can find clean content quickly. Velocita writes it, plus `llms-full.txt` with the full text, on every build.

## What it is not

It is not a ranking factor for Google, and AI crawlers are not required to read it. Treat it as a cheap, helpful extra, not a strategy.

## Signals that matter more

- **Clean, crawlable HTML** with real headings, which every page already has
- **Markdown copies** of each page, such as [this one](/blog/llms-txt-guide.md), for agents that prefer text
- **Structured data** that states facts explicitly
- **A clear crawler policy** with `aiCrawlers: 'allow' | 'search-only' | 'block'`

See the full list in [SEO and AI search](/docs/seo/), or read [why zero JavaScript is a feature](/blog/zero-js-is-a-feature/).

---

# Velocita 1.0 is here
URL: https://6t9xstar.github.io/velocita/blog/velocita-1-0/

## What's new

Velocita 1.0 completes the road from "fast by default" to "stays fast in production":

- **Starter templates** for a blog, docs and a local business, each scoring Lighthouse 100 in every category
- **`velocita deploy`** for Cloudflare Pages, Netlify, Vercel and GitHub Pages
- **`velocita check`**, a browser-free performance budget that runs in milliseconds
- **A Lighthouse CI gate** written for you, failing CI below 95

## Why a budget matters

Sites rarely start slow; they get slow one dependency at a time. A budget that runs on every build turns "we should keep it fast" into a failing check. Read more in [why zero JavaScript is a feature](/blog/zero-js-is-a-feature/).

## Get it

Follow [Getting started](/docs/), or pick a [template](/templates/).

---

# Why zero JavaScript is a feature
URL: https://6t9xstar.github.io/velocita/blog/zero-js-is-a-feature/

## The cost you don't see

Every kilobyte of JavaScript is downloaded, parsed, compiled and executed before a page becomes fully responsive. On a mid-range phone that cost shows up directly in Interaction to Next Paint.

## What content sites actually need

Most pages of a blog, docs site or marketing site are text, images and links. HTML already does that perfectly. The few interactive parts, such as search, a copy button or a calculator, can be [islands](/docs/islands/) that load on their own.

## Measuring it

The [home page](/) runs a live meter that shows its own transfer size, JavaScript weight and Largest Contentful Paint in your browser. Then try [the 1.0 release notes](/blog/velocita-1-0/) to see what keeps those numbers low over time.

---

# Configuration
URL: https://6t9xstar.github.io/velocita/docs/configuration/

## Site

```js
export default {
  title: 'My Site',
  description: 'What the site is about',
  url: 'https://example.com',   // a path here (/repo) is handled for you
  lang: 'en',
  nav: [{ title: 'Blog', url: '/blog/' }],
};
```

## Output profiles

`profile` picks which optional files a build writes. The default, `full`, builds the same files as earlier versions.

| Profile | What is emitted |
|---|---|
| `minimal` | HTML with meta tags and JSON-LD, sitemap.xml, robots.txt, `_headers`, search index |
| `standard` | `minimal` plus RSS and JSON feeds (site, sections, tags), OG images, responsive images |
| `ai` | `standard` plus a Markdown mirror of every page, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt` |
| `full` (default) | Everything. Today this is the same as `ai`; future optional output goes here |

```js
export default { profile: 'minimal', feed: true }; // explicit options override the profile
```

Measured with `node bench/bench.mjs 1000,5000 3 minimal,standard,ai,full`. The corpus is the bench's generated Markdown posts with `ogImages: false` and no `sharp`, so the image settings change nothing here. Times are medians of 3 runs on Node 24, i7-12800H, Windows 11. Other work was running on the machine, so treat the times as relative to each other. Astro 7.4 writes 28.5 MB for the same 5,000 posts.

| 5,000 posts | Output | Files | Clean build | No-op rebuild | Edit one post |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `minimal` | 63.5 MB | 5,740 | 9.1 s | 2.8 s | 3.0 s |
| `standard` | 69.2 MB | 5,784 | 9.2 s | 3.0 s | 3.1 s |
| `ai` / `full` | 101.9 MB | 10,787 | 8.7–9.7 s | 2.7–2.9 s | 3.0–3.7 s |

| 1,000 posts | Output | Files | Clean build |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `minimal` | 12.7 MB | 1,160 | 1.3 s |
| `standard` | 17.4 MB | 1,204 | 1.4 s |
| `ai` / `full` | 23.9 MB | 2,207 | 1.5–1.6 s |

Markdown mirrors and `llms-full.txt` account for about a third of the `full` output. Build time barely changes between profiles: rendering the HTML dominates.

## Behaviour

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `pageSize` | `20` | Items per list page |
| `aiCrawlers` | `'allow'` | `'search-only'` or `'block'` AI bots in robots.txt |
| `locales` | `[lang]` | Extra languages live in `content/<lang>/` |
| `sections` | `{}` | Per-folder layout and type, e.g. docs |
| `collections` | `{}` | Per-folder frontmatter schemas, see [content](/docs/content/#collection-schemas) |
| `budget` | 30/20/20 KB | Page, JS and CSS limits for `velocita check` |
| `indexNowKey` | none | Enables `--indexnow` pings. 8–128 characters of `a-z A-Z 0-9 -` |
| `contentSignal` | `false` | Adds a Content-Signal line to robots.txt (Lighthouse reports it as unknown) |
| `html` | `true` | Render raw HTML in Markdown and `.html` content. `false` escapes it on every page |
| `cache` | `true` | Persistent Markdown render cache in `.velocita-cache/` |
| `markdownMirror` / `llms` / `feed` | `true` | Markdown copy of each page, llms.txt files, RSS + JSON Feed |
| `ogImages` | `true` | Generated 1200×630 social cards (needs `sharp`) |
| `redirects` | `{}` | `{ '/old/': '/new/' }` → `_redirects` 301s + HTML fallbacks |

## Content sources

Pages can come from a headless CMS or any API as well as from `content/`:

```js
import { defineConfig, fromContentful, fromSanity, fromJson } from 'velocita';

export default defineConfig({
  sources: [
    fromContentful({ space: '…', accessToken: process.env.CONTENTFUL_TOKEN, contentType: 'post', section: 'blog' }),
    fromSanity({ projectId: '…', query: '*[_type=="post"]{title,"slug":slug.current,description,date,body}' }),
    fromJson({ url: 'https://api.example.com/posts.json', section: 'news' }),
  ],
});
```

A source is just `async (site) => [{ path: 'blog/x.md', data: { title, … }, body: 'markdown' }]`, so any API can become one. Each adapter accepts `map(item)` to fit your content model. Source pages get everything file pages get: SEO tags, feeds, OG images and the audit.

### Trusted and untrusted HTML

Content is trusted by default: raw HTML in Markdown (and `.html` pages) is copied into the page as written, which is what you want for your own files. If editors you don't fully trust can write CMS content, mark those entries `trusted: false` and their raw HTML is escaped as text, while Markdown still renders:

```js
fromJson({ url: 'https://api.example.com/posts.json', map: item => ({ path: `blog/${item.slug}.md`, data: item, body: item.body, trusted: false }) })
```

Set `html: false` in config to do the same for every page. In all modes, Markdown links and images with `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `file:` or non-image `data:` URLs become `#`, and `canonical`, `image` and other head URLs must be `http(s)` or site paths, or the build fails.

Next: write your own [layouts](/docs/layouts/).

---

# Content and routing
URL: https://6t9xstar.github.io/velocita/docs/content/

## Files become URLs

```
content/index.md          → /
content/about.md          → /about/
content/blog/hello.md     → /blog/hello/
content/hi/about.md       → /hi/about/   (second locale)
```

A folder is a collection. Dated files inside it become articles with an automatic index page, tag pages, feeds and pagination.

## Frontmatter

```yaml
---
title: Why speed matters        # under 60 characters
description: One-line summary   # under 160 characters
date: 2026-10-20
tags: [seo, performance]
image: /og/custom.png           # otherwise a card is generated
aliases: [/old-url/]            # 301 redirects
draft: true                     # excluded from production
---
```

All supported fields:

| Field | What it does |
|---|---|
| `updated` | Last-modified date for `dateModified`, the sitemap and feeds |
| `seoTitle` | A longer `<title>`; nav and `<h1>` keep `title` |
| `keywords` | `<meta name="keywords">` (falls back to tags) |
| `permalink` | Custom URL, e.g. `/custom/url/`. Must start with `/`; `..`, spaces, quotes, `<>`, `?` and `#` fail the build |
| `layout` | Layout name from `layouts/` |
| `noindex` | `robots: noindex`, and excluded from the sitemap and llms.txt |
| `translationKey` | Links translations whose paths differ |
| `faq` | `- Question? :: Answer.` list → FAQPage JSON-LD |
| `schema: HowTo` | With `steps` (`- Name :: What to do.`) and `totalTime` (e.g. `PT5M`) |
| `schema: Product` | With `price`, `currency`, `brand`, `sku`, `rating`, `reviewCount`, `availability` |
| `video` | VideoObject JSON-LD, with `videoThumbnail` and `videoDuration` |

Frontmatter is a YAML subset: strings, numbers, booleans, `[a, b]` arrays, `- item` lists, and nested maps and lists by indentation:

```yaml
author:
  name: Ada
  links:
    - https://ada.example
sponsors:
  - name: Acme
    tier: gold
```

## Collection schemas

Give a folder a schema in `velocita.config.js` and every file in it is checked at build time:

```js
export default {
  collections: {
    blog: {
      schema: {
        title: 'string',              // required
        date: 'date',
        tags: 'string[]?',            // ? = optional
        draft: 'boolean?',
        rating: { type: 'number', required: false, validate: v => (v >= 1 && v <= 5) || 'must be 1–5' },
      },
    },
  },
};
```

Types are `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `date` (a parseable date) and `string[]`. `validate(value, data)` runs when the value is present; return `false` or a message to reject it. Fields not in the schema are allowed. All mismatches are reported together and fail the build:

```
Frontmatter does not match the collection schema:
  blog/hello.md: field "date" is required (date) by collections.blog.schema
  blog/old.md: field "rating": must be 1–5
```

Two pages with the same URL (for example `blog/Hello.md` and `blog/hello.md`, or a clashing `permalink`) also fail the build, naming both files.

## Images

Write `![Alt text](photo.jpg)` with the file next to the Markdown. Velocita copies it, adds width and height, and creates WebP sizes when `sharp` is installed.

Continue with [configuration](/docs/configuration/).

---

# Deploy
URL: https://6t9xstar.github.io/velocita/docs/deploy/

## Generate host config

```bash
velocita deploy init cloudflare   # wrangler.toml
velocita deploy init netlify      # netlify.toml
velocita deploy init vercel       # vercel.json with headers and redirects
velocita deploy init github       # GitHub Actions workflow
```

Each also writes `lighthouserc.json`, which fails CI if any Lighthouse category drops below 95.

## Publish

```bash
velocita deploy cloudflare
```

This builds, stops on broken links or a blown performance budget, and then publishes with the host's own CLI.

## Subfolders

If `url` has a path, such as `https://user.github.io/repo`, every internal link is prefixed for you. This site is deployed that way.

Back to [Getting started](/docs/).

---

# Multilingual sites
URL: https://6t9xstar.github.io/velocita/docs/i18n/

## Configure locales

```js
export default {
  lang: 'en',
  locales: ['en', 'hi'],
  nav: { en: [/* … */], hi: [/* … */] },
};
```

## Add translations

`content/about.md` and `content/hi/about.md` are linked as translations automatically. For different file names, give both the same `translationKey`.

Every translated page gets `hreflang` tags with `x-default`, sitemap alternates, the right `<html lang>`, and a switcher in the header. Feeds and search work per language.

Last step: [deploy your site](/docs/deploy/).

---

# Getting started
URL: https://6t9xstar.github.io/velocita/docs/

## Requirements

- Node.js 20 or newer
- Optional: `sharp` for responsive images and generated social cards

## Create a site

```bash
npm create velocita@latest my-site -- --template blog
cd my-site
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open `http://localhost:3000`. Edit any file in `content/`, `layouts/`, `public/` (or the folders `contentDir`, `layoutsDir` and `publicDir` point to), `velocita.config.js` or a local theme, and the page reloads. If a rebuild fails, the server keeps running: the error is printed in the terminal and shown in the browser, and the page reloads once you fix it.

Something not working? `npx velocita doctor` checks your Node.js version, that the config and themes load, that the configured folders exist, and whether `sharp` is installed. It exits with code 1 if anything is broken.

## Build for production

```bash
npm run build      # velocita build --strict
npx velocita check # performance budget
```

The output in `dist/` is plain static files. Rebuilds are incremental: only files whose content changed are written.

To look at the production build before deploying, run `npx velocita preview`. It serves `dist/` exactly as built on `http://127.0.0.1:4173` (change with `--port` and `--host`), without rebuilding or live reload.

## Next steps

Learn how [content is organised](/docs/content/), then see every [configuration option](/docs/configuration/).

---

# Islands and search
URL: https://6t9xstar.github.io/velocita/docs/islands/

## Write an island

```js
// islands/counter.js
export default function counter(el, { start = 0 }) {
  el.innerHTML = '<button>0</button>';
}
```

## Use it in Markdown

```html
<v-island name="counter" load="visible" props='{"start":3}'>Fallback HTML</v-island>
```

| `load` | Loads when |
|---|---|
| `visible` | It scrolls into view (default) |
| `idle` | The browser is idle |
| `interaction` | First hover, focus or touch |
| `load` | Immediately |

Only pages with an island get the small loader. The install box and the live performance meter on the [home page](/) are islands.

## Search

`/search/` is generated for every language. It is a small island over a prebuilt index, so it needs no server or third-party service.

Next: [multilingual sites](/docs/i18n/).

---

# Layouts
URL: https://6t9xstar.github.io/velocita/docs/layouts/

## A layout is a function

```js
// layouts/post.js
export default ({ page, site, articles, h }) => `
  <article>
    <h1>${h.escape(page.title)}</h1>
    ${page.html}
  </article>`;
```

Files in `layouts/` replace the built-in `page`, `post`, `list`, `search` and `notFound` layouts, or add new ones you choose with `layout:` in frontmatter.

## Helpers

| Helper | Use |
|---|---|
| `h.escape(text)` | Escape text for HTML |
| `h.date(date, lang)` | Accessible `<time>` element |
| `h.pager(page.pagination)` | Pagination links |
| `h.css(extra)` | Base theme CSS plus yours, minified |

## The shell

`layouts/shell.js` controls the whole document. This website uses a custom shell for its header and footer.

See [SEO and AI search](/docs/seo/) for what goes into `<head>` automatically.

---

# SEO and AI search
URL: https://6t9xstar.github.io/velocita/docs/seo/

## On every page

- Title, description, canonical and robots meta
- Open Graph and Twitter cards with a generated 1200×630 image
- JSON-LD: WebSite, BreadcrumbList, BlogPosting, plus FAQPage, HowTo, Product, VideoObject and LocalBusiness when you use them

## Site-wide files

`sitemap.xml` with hreflang alternates, `robots.txt`, RSS and JSON feeds, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, and a `.md` copy of every page for AI agents.

## The audit

```bash
velocita audit
```

Reports broken internal links and `#anchors`, orphan pages, duplicate titles and descriptions, and suggests related posts to link. `velocita build --strict` fails on errors.

## IndexNow

Set `indexNowKey`, then `velocita build --indexnow` notifies Bing, Yandex and others about only the URLs that changed.

Next: add interactivity with [islands](/docs/islands/).

---

# Themes
URL: https://6t9xstar.github.io/velocita/docs/themes/

Browse the [theme gallery](/themes/) to see each theme in light and dark.

## Use a theme

```sh
npm install velocita-theme-paper
```

```js
// velocita.config.js
export default { theme: 'velocita-theme-paper' };
```

`theme` can be an npm package name, a local file (`'./themes/brand.js'`), an inline object, or an array of these. Later themes override earlier ones.

## What wins

| Setting | Order (last wins) |
|---|---|
| Config | Velocita defaults → theme `config` → your `velocita.config.js` |
| Layouts | built-in → theme `layouts` → your `layouts/` folder |
| CSS | built-in theme CSS → theme `css` → your `css` |

## Write a theme

A theme is a module whose default export is an object:

```js
export default {
  name: 'brand',
  config: { themeColor: '#9c3d10', og: { accent: '#9c3d10' } }, // defaults the site can override
  css: `:root{--accent:#9c3d10} body{font-family:Georgia,serif}`,
  layouts: {
    // Same signature as files in layouts/: { page, site, pages, articles, sections, tags, h }
    list: ({ page, site, h }) => `<h1>${h.escape(page.title)}</h1>
      <ul>${page.items.map(p => `<li><a href="${p.url}">${h.escape(p.title)}</a></li>`).join('')}</ul>
      ${h.pager(page.pagination)}`,
  },
  // shell: ({ page, site, head, content }) => '<!doctype html>…', // optional: replace the whole page shell
};
```

To share it, publish it to npm as `velocita-theme-<name>` with the `velocita-theme` keyword and `velocita` as a peer dependency. [`packages/velocita-theme-paper`](https://github.com/6t9xstar/velocita/tree/main/packages/velocita-theme-paper) is a complete example.

Layouts must escape user content with `h.escape`, and should keep pages free of scripts so the zero-JS guarantee and `velocita check` still hold.

## Create a site

```bash
npm create velocita@latest                # asks for folder, template and title
npm create velocita@latest my-site -- --template docs --title "Acme Docs"
cd my-site
npm install
npm run dev
```

## Measured, not promised

Each template was built and run through Lighthouse CI on every page:

| Template | Performance | Accessibility | Best practices | SEO |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Blog | 100 | 100 | 100 | 100 |
| Docs | 100 | 100 | 100 | 100 |
| Local business | 100 | 100 | 100 | 100 |
| News / magazine | 100 | 100 | 100 | 100 |
| Agency / portfolio | 100 | 100 | 100 | 100 |

News and portfolio were measured on November 1, 2026 across all 16 pages of each starter (`@lhci/cli` 0.14, Lighthouse's default mobile emulation with simulated throttling). Largest Contentful Paint stayed under 1.3 s and layout shift under 0.005 on every page. Pages marked `noindex` (404, search, and tag pages with a single post) score 66 for SEO by design, because Lighthouse counts `noindex` against them.

Next, read [Getting started](/docs/) or learn how to [deploy](/docs/deploy/).

## Use a theme

```bash
npm install velocita-theme-paper
```

```js
// velocita.config.js
export default {
  theme: 'velocita-theme-paper',
  // Anything you set here overrides the theme's defaults.
};
```

The previews above use each theme's real colors and fonts. Theme CSS is inlined like the default theme's, so switching themes never adds a render-blocking request.

## Publish your own

1. Export a plain object `{ name, config, css, layouts }` from your package's `index.js`. See the [themes guide](/docs/themes/) for every field.
2. Name the package `velocita-theme-<name>` and add the `velocita-theme` keyword.
3. Check that a site using it still passes `velocita audit` and `velocita check`.
4. Publish it to npm, then [open an issue on GitHub](https://github.com/6t9xstar/velocita/issues/new?title=Theme%20gallery%3A%20) to get it listed here.
